source.quote: Greetings travelers and welcome back to Goldbound, the challenge series where we're farming our way through Azeroth one zone at a time. In each new zone we explore, uncover some of the best and some of the worst gold farms until we've earned enough gold to buy a WoW token. Then, and only then, can we spin the randomizer for a new zone. In last episode, we entered into Thousand Needles, blitzed through some of the best transmog and dungeon farms in the series so far, the likes of the Saltstone Cave and Razorfen Downs. But, transmog sales were kind of slow and we left off with a mailbox clear shooting us just under 200,000 gold, which isn't quite enough because the WoW token has been hovering around 260,000 gold lately. I have had a few extra days to keep items listed, try to do some undercuts, and even skin a few more turtles. Let's go ahead and see where things are sitting at at the moment because who knows, we could have a new zone spin sooner than expected.

source.quote: First and foremost, check out this guy, Mad Megus Turth, who is up at Turth's haunt here over in the far east of the zone. He hangs around the blue casting circle and once we take him out, we actually get what is either a ghost of his past or someone whose enchantments are no longer working on, aka a vendor, who just so happens to sell Ancona chickens, a battle pet. Now, the base version of this pet here only sells for about 50 to 100 gold, but the purchase price is only one gold. So, really not a bad markup. Plus, if we learn the chicken into our battle pet log and then put it into a cage, we do get the caged version, which is a different auction house listing and actually has a market value closer to about 200 to 800 gold.

source.quote: So, let's keep it rolling. Now that I think of it though, there are a few other little things in the zone that could bring in some more gold, like this rare, Iron Eye, a basilisk. Much like a few other mobs in the zone, he has a pretty notable weapon drop on his loot table, the Blade of the Basilisk. This one-handed sword has a market value of about 30,000 gold, so it is definitely worth tagging. That being said, he is one of the more regularly camped rares in the zone, so it can be a bit harder to get consistent tags on him, especially since we're usually down in the waters going after the turtle spawns. Speaking of zones though, and since we're in the final leg of farming for the WoW token, let's Let's about what zones we can actually roll for.

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/037 - I Finally Rolled A Death Zone - Goldbound 36.en-orig.txt
source.quote: Oh, the Hinterlands, the archaeology haven. Well, let's go. For this one, the best path that we have, and well, the only path we have into the Hinterlands is actually through a Raff Basin. There's a tunnel here that heads straight up into Hinterlands. So, let's go on in. There we go. A brand new zone to explore, and might I say, a nice change of scenery. It's looking somewhere between Elwynn Forest and Grizzly Hills, fine by me. So, this zone is actually a little bit of a smaller one compared to some of our recent unlocks, but we do have a few key areas, like the dwarf stronghold of Aerie Peak, the forested roads, home to owlkin and wolves, the North Quel'Thalas Lodge, a high elf stronghold, plus the Glen of Seradane. Then down to the south, we have a variety of troll ruins, like the Altar of Zul, Jintha'Alor, Revantusk Village, and of course, over on the shore, turtles. Will the turtle meta return? We'll just have to see. First and foremost, there is one thing on my mind, well, three things actually, the archaeology dig sites. So, let's get digging. Now, archaeology might not normally be that interesting to most retail players, but in a zone locked challenge like Goldbound, it opens up the table to a whole new variety of zone-based luck. Because on each continent, there's always four archaeology dig sites up, meaning, whenever one dig site is completed, it forces one to spawn in one of the other archaeology sites in one of the other zones on the continent. Although, the game doesn't know which zones we have unlocked. So, until we have every single Eastern Kingdom zone available, the dig sites will eventually spawn into locked zones, which is exactly what happened the first day we unlocked archaeology when all of the dig sites pretty much went to Hinterlands. Lucky for us, it means we have three fresh chances to run through this. As far as archaeology goes, we can get some nice upgrades like the Raptor mount, but also for Goldie, archaeology is some of the highest XP per hour that we can get. For example, we've spent almost 5 days played, or 125 hours to get halfway through level 84 so far, but each of the archaeology tablets, which you get about six per dig site, gives us 6,000 XP, at least while we're rested.

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/037 - I Finally Rolled A Death Zone - Goldbound 36.en-orig.txt
source.quote: Usually we get our own soul bound artifacts, but sometimes we get a rare tradeable version. These can be used artifact crafts for troll or dwarf fragments, but for us, we can also sell them on the auction house to other players to use in their crafts. And over the two hours of farming, I got seven troll fragments worth about 300 to 500 gold each. On top of that, two dwarf runes worth 200 to 400 gold each. So about 3.1 thousand gold for the tradeable fragments, but that's not all because in the end, I actually procced a rare troll archaeology craft. It takes a hundred of our troll fragments to craft and it gives us the voodoo figurine, which we can learn, promptly put into a cage, and then sell on the auction house for upwards of 9,000 gold. Yep. So all in all, with vendor items included, we pulled in about 12,200 gold for two hours of archaeology, working out to about 6,100 gold per hour. A good chunk of that was the pet, which very well may just be dumb luck and the actual gold per hour might be a lot lower, but hey, at least for our sample size here, we'll call that some good gold per hour from archaeology. On top of the archaeology loot though, since we were covering such large distances across the whole continent, I did have track treasure on. I actually found quite a few treasure chests. From the chests in Hinterlands, which just so happened to have a lot of archaeology sites and a lot of chests, I got a few things. First up, the Archaic Defender, an absolute gem of a transmog find and one that we shouldn't have trouble selling over the next couple weeks or months because it has both a solid market value of about 60,000 gold but also a super clean appearance.

source.quote: And then from the assorted chest that I saw while flying between dig sites, I pulled in three more blues. The Twisted Chanter's Staff, about 3 to 4,000 gold. The Shield of Thorson, about 6 to 12,000 gold. And the Drake Wind Bands, about 9,000 gold. So all in all, on top of archaeology, we got some pretty insane market value just flying around Eastern Kingdoms. But we're in Hinterlands after all, so let's get after some regular zone farms. There is one that I think we should test out first because we still have skinning leveled up from Thousand Needles and I did happen to see some turtles on the west coast of the Hinterlands here, the Saltwater Snapjaws. These guys are spread across the shores just past the Overlook Cliffs and a few of them are even hanging out in the water. So what do we do? We farm them. As I'm testing it out here, there are two main issues.

source.quote: Seeing as we're in a pretty high level zone though, I think the turtle meta may be failing here. So let's get on to some other farms, which we do actually have a few notable vendors in the zone to frequent and try to flip some of their wares. The closest one to our current location on the shore is just up the hills here over in the Stormfeather Outpost with some dwarves. The one that we want in particular, none other than Brannick Ironbelly. He has a ton of white items, which actually have pretty reasonable market values for the plate mail and brigandine sets. Plus, he also has some limited supply greens that we can snag. These ones are in the two to five thousand gold range, so it is definitely worth stopping by Brannick a few times a day to try to pick these up.

source.quote: Then on to the other vendors. So, if we head up over to the northeast of the Kvaldir Lodge, there's actually a little gnome lookout here. And inside of it, Rupo Zipcoil. He has a few limited supply engineering recipes like the Mithril Mechanical Dragonling. These sell for a few thousand gold in the auction house, but only cost us about 40 silver, which isn't a bad markup. And outside, his business associate, Gidget, can have a few items as well. But, it looks like his stock is sold out at the moment. Now, that isn't all the vendors in the zone, but I might keep another one on the down low for a little bit longer to hopefully choose one of few sales. With that, we do have a marginal farm on the turtles and a few decent little vendor flips to try out.

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/037 - I Finally Rolled A Death Zone - Goldbound 36.en-orig.txt
source.quote: But, with our archaeology sites all locked away and still no solid consistent farm, things are looking kind of grim in the Hinterlands. So, when in doubt, let's do a gather. I will have to drop my skinning here to go level mining up to about 200 to get the full ranks for the ores here. But, luckily we pretty much have herbalism still maxed out from Thousand Needles, so it doesn't take too long to get to speed and to get testing. The area of the zone is pretty small here in the Hinterlands. Not to mention, there is no Vis a Dormi to swap time phases here to try to reset nodes. So, we are running into a little bit of an herb and ore shortage. It isn't anything too crazy, but it definitely feels like we can loop around the zone faster than the herbs and ores respawn. So, I think down the road in this zone, there may be an optimized route that loops into another zone, like Arathi, just so we have a bigger route to give the nodes more time to spawn. As far as the Hinterlands yield for herbs though, there's quite a big variety. The big one being Goldthorn, a classic high-value herb in the series, but then also a few blindweed spawns. Mostly around the lakes and the troll camps, and this is a minor unlock for the challenge. We haven't really had any blindweed readily available in our previous zones. It's only worth about eight gold each, but it's definitely a good resource to have access to. And there was one more herb that I was hoping to get here, the ghost mushroom.
source.canonical_file: goldbound/037 - I Finally Rolled A Death Zone - Goldbound 36.en-orig.txt

source.quote: As for ore, we only pulled in 84 iron ore and some really low amounts of gold and silver. So, a really small yield here, and all of this only adds up to a total gold per hour of 3,400. Still better than turtle farming here, but not exactly the juiciest farm to get us out of the zone anytime soon. Here is where the gold stacks up. We only have just under 400 raw gold from the zone so far, but the WoW token has dropped back down to 250k, so a lower target. As for the mailbox, well on Goldie here, we do have a few trade goods moving, but we haven't really gotten stuck into any one farm for too long. And the farms we have done, well they're not too good. So I'll loot this up and see where we fall.
